subject: Offramp orchestration & auto-renew exception proposal
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Tim Patel <tim@polarishealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@polarishealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Offramp orchestration & auto-renew exception proposal

Hi Tim / Polaris procurement team,

Thanks again for the productive call last week. As discussed, we want to make the off-ramp mechanics explicit in the MSA + Order Form so your procurement and legal teams can sign without additional back-and-forth. Attached are two redlines (MSA and Order Form) showing the changes we believe address your concerns. High-level summary of the proposal: 

- Auto-renew: keep auto-renew but add explicit proactive reminders at 75 and 45 days before renewal and a one-click opt-out link.
- Notice window: accept mutual 45-day notice for termination (both parties) in lieu of a longer 60-day window, conditioned on the opt-out reminders above.
- Termination for convenience (TFC): mutual TFC with pro-rated service credit instead of an exit fee. We propose wording that limits credit to unused committed capacity, not future credits.
- Transition: Redwood commits to a 30-day handoff support period (operational runbook + access handover) for customers exercising termination.

Key asks from Polaris we captured: clarity on notice timing, whether TFC carries a repayment/fee, and assurances about data handoff. The attached redlines reflect a compromise: faster notice (45d) in exchange for a capped pro-rated credit and a standard handoff SLA.

Please review the two attachments. If this looks directionally correct, can your legal team flag any absolute blockers? If not, we’ll prepare a final DocuSign-ready orderform with the acceptance fields prefilled.

Attachments: MSA_redline_20260602.pdf (annotated), OrderForm_v3_redline.docx

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Tim Patel <tim@polarishealth.com>

Cc: polaris-legal@polarishealth.com
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Offramp orchestration & auto-renew exception proposal

Hannah — thanks for the summary and the redlines. A couple quick notes from our side after an initial read: 

1) Notice window: 45 days is preferable to your 60-day ask, but given internal approval cycles we usually require 45 days minimum. Are you able to commit to the reminder cadence you mentioned? If we don’t see a reminder, we’ll push for 60 days.
2) TFC: we are not comfortable with a unilateral credit; we prefer a negotiated exit fee or mutual pro-rated credit. We need to understand how you calculate the credit (start/end dates, committed vs used).
3) Data handoff: we need confirmation that logs and audit artifacts will remain available for 90 days after termination.

We’ll escalate to Polaris legal for redline feedback; appreciate if Redwood legal can provide a short clause-level explanation to speed our review.

—Tim
Tim Patel
Head of Procurement, Polaris Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tim Patel <tim@polarishealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Offramp orchestration & auto-renew exception proposal

Tim / Hannah — quick legal view to unblock. Appreciate the clear asks. My suggested approach (included as redline text in the attached MSA):

- Notice window: mutual 45-day notice to terminate. We will add an explicit Definitions/Notice clause clarifying when notice is "received" (email to designated procurement/contract mailbox) and confirm Redwood’s reminder cadence (automated at 75/45 days plus delivery receipt logs available on request).
- TFC mechanics: convert to mutual termination for convenience with a pro-rated credit equal to the unused portion of pre-paid committed capacity (calculated on a 30-day month basis). No clawbacks on consumed credits. This is narrower than an exit fee; it should be acceptable commercially and cap Redwood’s exposure.
- Data retention: Redwood will retain access logs and transaction audit artifacts for 90 days post-termination, and provide an export package on request within 15 business days.

Proposed clause snippet (for legal to review):
"Upon mutual termination for convenience, customer shall receive a pro-rated credit for prepaid, unused committed capacity, calculated from the effective date of termination to the end of the prepaid period. Redwood shall not be required to issue credits for usage already consumed. Redwood will retain operational and audit logs for 90 days and will provide an export upon Customer request within 15 business days."

If Polaris legal wants a formal redline change rather than notes, we can convert this to tracked changes and re-upload.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tim Patel <tim@polarishealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Offramp orchestration & auto-renew exception proposal

Tim — quick commercial context from our side: 45-day notice in exchange for the pro-rated credit is workable for us for the pilot and Standard tiers. For larger committed deals we usually hold 60 days, but we can include a carveout in the Order Form so this 45-day mutual notice applies to the initial term only (and reverts to 60d auto thereafter). That gives Polaris the flexibility you need now without locking Redwood into recurring shorter windows.

If that’s acceptable, I’ll update the Order Form language.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Team — operational checklist to make the 45-day compromise reliable: 

- Automate reminders: set system triggers for 75 and 45 days; reminders written to procurement mailbox with read receipts logged in the contract audit trail.
- DocuSign flow: prepare an Order Form template that references the MSA redline and exposes the opt-out link in the acceptance panel.
- Reporting: create a short Renewal Report for Polaris that shows committed capacity vs consumption 90/60/30 day snapshots.
- Handoff runbook: prepare a 30-day offboarding runbook (tasks, roles, SRE contacts) and attach as an SOW appendix.

I’ve attached a draft SOW checklist and the updated OrderForm_v3_redline.docx. Proposed timeline: internal sign-off by 06/07, share final with Polaris legal by 06/08, request signature by 06/15.

—Aditya

Tim / Polaris legal — thanks for the quick turn. Based on the internal alignment above, Redwood proposes the following final path forward: 

1) MSA: mutual 45-day notice to terminate for convenience for the initial term only; reverts to 60-day notice on any renewal term unless otherwise agreed in a signed Order Form.
2) TFC: mutual pro-rated credit for unused pre-paid committed capacity (calculated monthly), no clawback for consumed credits.
3) Data: 90-day retention for logs and a 15-business-day export window.
4) Operational safeguards: automated 75/45 day reminders to the procurement mailbox, DocuSign-ready Order Form with opt-out link, 30-day handoff runbook attached as SOW appendix.

I have attached the MSA_redline_20260602.pdf with tracked changes and the OrderForm_v3_redline.docx. If Polaris is okay with this, can you confirm by next Wednesday (2026-06-09)? We’ll then push the updated DocuSign package and the HubSpot deal will be moved to "Contracting - Final" (link below).
